The test image shows a tomato plant in the center that has completely collapsed/wilted — leaves are drooping, the whole plant has fallen, while surrounding plants are healthy. This is a whole-plant wilt symptom. The leaves appear still greenish (not yellowed), suggesting rapid sudden wilt rather than slow vascular disease.

Key candidates: Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Bacterial_Wilt, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Southern_Blight.

No white fungal mats visible at the base (rules out Southern_Blight), no mosaic pattern (rules out CMV). The sudden complete collapse with green leaves is classic for bacterial wilt. I'll use my 1 reference image to confirm Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.

The reference image is an extremely strong visual match to the test image:
- Both show complete whole-plant wilt/collapse on black plastic mulch
- Both show drooping green leaves with total plant collapse
- Same commercial tomato field setting
- Even the Bugwood image numbers are consecutive (5593858 test vs 5593860 reference), suggesting same photo series

The symptom description for Southern_Bacterial_Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum) — sudden plant collapse, permanent wilt, vascular discoloration — perfectly fits this presentation.
